title: ADDENDUM TO INFORMATION — General Jennie Carignan, Chief of the Defence Staff
legal_basis: Criminal Code of Canada, s.504 — Private prosecution by information laid before a Justice of the Peace

respondent.name: General Jennie Carignan, CMM, MSC, CD
respondent.position: Chief of the Defence Staff, Canadian Armed Forces
respondent.appointed_by: Governor in Council on recommendation of Minister of National Defence

charges.offence: Breach of Trust by Public Officer
charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan, being a public officer entrusted with command of the Canadian Armed Forces, did commit a breach of trust by: (a) permitting the defunding of the CAF retention program while acknowledging retention as the core personnel crisis; (b) signing a mobilization directive targeting 400,000 while internal DND documents confirm systems are at capacity; (c) failing to maintain force readiness with 76% of occupations at 10%+ shortfall.
sources: CBC — CDS testimony on retention (2024)
CBC — Retention program defunding (2025)
Auditor General Spring 2026 — CAF Recruiting Audit
DND internal documents (July 2025) — capacity assessment

charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan did acts prejudicial to the safety, security or defence of Canada by: (a) allowing CAF strength to fall to 88,715 against an authorized establishment of 101,500; (b) maintaining 2,000+ personnel on foreign rotation in Latvia while domestic force hollows; (c) permitting a training bottleneck of 6,400/year that makes the 400,000 mobilization target mathematically impossible (62.5 years at current rate).
sources: Auditor General Report 2025 — CAF strength data
DND Departmental Plan 2026-27
CBC — Training bottleneck testimony

charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan behaved before the enemy in such a manner as to show cowardice by: (a) surrendering the digital battle space that CAF doctrine identifies as contested ground; (b) restricting public engagement on official CAF channels while establishing Cyber Command to nominally contest the information domain; (c) failing to publicly defend CAF members or Canadian citizens against identified threats.
sources: CAF Joint Doctrine Note 2017-01 — Information Operations
Thompson Current — CDS on cyber threats
DAOD 2008-8 — Social media policy

charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan, being an officer, did ill-treat persons subordinate to her by: (a) maintaining a training system that causes months of underemployment driving attrition; (b) defunding the retention program that addressed member welfare; (c) addressing only 65 of the Culture Implementation Plan recommendations while withholding culture survey data.
sources: CBC — Training bottleneck causing underemployment
Global News — Culture reform progress
DND leaked internal report (April 2025) — recruit underemployment

charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan negligently performed her duty as CDS by: (a) failing to meet recruitment and training targets between April 2022 and March 2025 (AG finding); (b) allowing attrition to rise from 4,256 to 5,026 departures year-over-year; (c) processing 192,000 applications but recruiting only 15,000 (1 in 13) with 250-day average processing time.
sources: Auditor General Report 2025
The Hub — Military recruitment crisis analysis (Feb 2026)
Global News — Retention/recruitment crisis

charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan disobeyed lawful command by failing to execute the Crown's obligation to maintain adequate defence of Canadian sovereignty while: (a) prioritizing NATO alliance obligations over domestic force readiness; (b) expanding foreign military access to Canadian territory (12 NATO nations at Suffield, Arctic training slots for allies) while CAF strength declines; (c) reversing course on mobilization commitments (public servant reserve recruitment).
sources: Canada.ca — Exercise Precise Response (12 nations, CFB Suffield)
CBC — Arctic expansion with allied training slots
Esprit de Corps — CDS reverses course on mobilization

charges.offence: Conduct to the Prejudice of Good Order and Discipline
charges.particulars: That Gen Carignan conducted herself in a manner prejudicial to good order and discipline by: (a) making public statements contradicted by subsequent actions (doublespeak pattern); (b) accepting appointment of DM Christiane Fox to DND despite Fox's documented COI Act breach; (c) failing to ensure the integrity of the DND command chain.
sources: Ethics Commissioner Report — Fox COI breach (April 2026)
PM.gc.ca — Fox appointment (Dec 2025)
CBC, Globe and Mail, Thompson Current — CDS public statements vs actions

filing_instructions.procedure: Criminal Code s.504 — Attend before a Justice of the Peace in any province with this information sworn under oath
filing_instructions.courts: Any superior court registry in Canada — see s504-court-filing.html for complete dispatch list
